question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-320, before the Department of Consumer Protection may investigate a real estate licensee based on a written complaint from a member of the public, what must that complaint (alone or together with supporting evidence) establish?
choice_a: Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
choice_b: A prima facie case
choice_c: A prior criminal conviction of the licensee
choice_d: Written consent from the licensee to be investigated
explanation: Section 20-320 authorizes the Department to investigate a licensee "upon the request of the commission or upon the verified complaint in writing of any person, if such complaint, or such complaint together with evidence, documentary or otherwise, presented in connection with such complaint, shall make out a prima facie case."

question: When the Connecticut Real Estate Commission finds, after proceedings under § 20-321, that a broker is guilty of a violation listed in § 20-320, what license actions is the Commission authorized to take?
choice_a: Only a permanent, non-appealable revocation
choice_b: Mandatory referral to a criminal court for sentencing
choice_c: Temporary suspension or permanent revocation of the license
choice_d: Automatic transfer of the license to another broker
explanation: Section 20-320 gives the Commission authority to "temporarily suspend or permanently revoke any license issued under the provisions of this chapter" upon a finding of a qualifying violation after a hearing under § 20-321.

question: In addition to, or instead of, suspending or revoking a license under § 20-320, the Commission may, in its discretion, impose a fine of not more than what amount?
explanation: Section 20-320 permits the Commission, "in addition to or in lieu of such suspension or revocation," to "impose a fine of not more than two thousand dollars" upon a qualifying finding.

question: Besides the specific list of prohibited acts, § 20-320 also lets the Commission suspend or revoke a license when it finds that the licensee did what?
choice_a: Obtained the license itself by false or fraudulent misrepresentation
choice_b: Failed to renew a license within 90 days of expiration
choice_c: Changed their mailing address without notifying the Commission
choice_d: Declined to join a local Realtor association
explanation: Section 20-320 applies when the Commission finds "that the licensee has by false or fraudulent misrepresentation obtained a license" — a separate basis from the thirteen enumerated grounds of post-licensure misconduct.

question: A Connecticut broker knowingly tells a buyer that a home's furnace was replaced last year, when the broker knows this is false, in order to induce the buyer to move forward with the purchase. Which § 20-320 ground for discipline does this describe?
choice_a: Commingling of funds
choice_b: Making a material misrepresentation
choice_c: Failure to provide required disclosures under § 20-325c
choice_d: Violating regulations adopted under the chapter
explanation: Section 20-320(1) lists "making any material misrepresentation" as a ground for suspension or revocation.

question: A broker tells a prospective seller, "I promise I can get you $50,000 over asking price if you list with me," knowing the promise is unfounded, purely to persuade the seller to sign a listing agreement. Which § 20-320 ground applies?
choice_a: Acting as agent for more than one party without knowledge of all parties
choice_b: Failing to account for or remit money belonging to others
choice_c: Making a false promise of a character likely to influence, persuade or induce
choice_d: Failing to deliver a copy of an instrument to a party executing it
explanation: Section 20-320(2) lists "making any false promise of a character likely to influence, persuade or induce" as an independent ground for discipline, distinct from a material misrepresentation about a fact.

question: A broker represents both the buyer and the seller in the same transaction but never tells either party that the other is also a client. Which § 20-320 ground for discipline is implicated?
choice_a: Collecting compensation in advance and failing to render an accounting
choice_b: Entering into an exclusive listing contract with an automatic continuation clause
choice_c: Conviction of a crime
choice_d: Acting as an agent for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom the licensee acts
explanation: Section 20-320(3) prohibits "acting as an agent for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge of all parties for whom the licensee acts" — i.e., undisclosed dual agency.

question: A licensed salesperson tells a buyer she can also represent them through a different broker across town, without ever telling her own employing/affiliated broker. Which § 20-320 ground does this violate?
choice_a: Representing or attempting to represent a real estate broker other than the licensee's employer or affiliated broker, without that employer's or broker's express knowledge and consent
choice_b: Making a material misrepresentation
choice_c: Violating a provision of the chapter or a regulation adopted under it
choice_d: Failing to provide disclosures required under § 20-325c
explanation: Section 20-320(4) makes it a disciplinary ground to represent or attempt to represent "a real estate broker other than the licensee's employer or the broker with whom the licensee is affiliated, without the express knowledge and consent of the licensee's employer or affiliated broker."

question: A broker receives a buyer's earnest money deposit and simply holds onto it for weeks without depositing it or accounting to anyone, well beyond what the situation requires. Which § 20-320 ground applies?
choice_a: Making a false promise of a character likely to induce
choice_b: Failing, within a reasonable time, to account for or remit any moneys coming into the licensee's possession which belong to others
choice_c: Entering an exclusive buyer agency contract with an automatic continuation clause
choice_d: Engaging in the business of real estate broker without a license
explanation: Section 20-320(5) makes it a ground for discipline to fail "within a reasonable time, to account for or remit any moneys coming into the licensee's possession which belong to others."

question: A broker asks a seller to sign an exclusive listing agreement that states a fixed one-year termination date, but also includes a clause automatically continuing the listing beyond that date without any new signature. Under § 20-320, this contract term is:
choice_a: Permitted as long as the commission rate does not change
choice_b: Only a problem if the seller objects in writing within 10 days
choice_c: A specific ground for suspension or revocation of the broker's license
choice_d: Permitted for buyer agency contracts but not listing contracts
explanation: Section 20-320(6) makes it a ground for discipline to enter "an exclusive listing contract or buyer agency contract which contains a fixed termination date if such contract also provides for an automatic continuation of the period of such contract beyond such date."

question: A broker prepares a lease under her supervision and has the tenant sign it, but does not give the tenant a copy for several days. Under § 20-320, what is the required timing for delivering a copy of an executed instrument to the party who signed it?
choice_a: Within 10 business days
choice_b: Within 30 calendar days
choice_c: Before the next scheduled showing
choice_d: Immediately
explanation: Section 20-320(7) makes it a disciplinary ground to fail "to deliver immediately a copy of any instrument to any party or parties executing the instrument" in connection with a real estate transaction the licensee prepared or supervised.

question: Among the enumerated grounds in § 20-320, which of the following is also listed as a basis for suspension or revocation, subject to the fair-chance considerations of Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46a-80?
choice_a: Conviction of a crime
choice_b: Failure to attend a Commission meeting
choice_c: Failure to join a multiple listing service
choice_d: Advertising a listing on a Sunday
explanation: Section 20-320(8) lists conviction of a crime as a ground for discipline, with the statute expressly cross-referencing the fair-chance/criminal-record consideration provisions of § 46a-80.
source_note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-320(8); Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46a-80

question: A broker collects a fee up front from a client for services she has not yet performed, and later fails to render an accounting of how that money was used. Which § 20-320 ground does this describe?
choice_a: Commingling funds of others with the licensee's own funds
choice_b: Collecting compensation in advance of services to be performed and failing to render an accounting
choice_c: Acting as agent for more than one party without knowledge of all parties
choice_d: Failing to deliver an instrument to the party executing it
explanation: Section 20-320(9) makes it a disciplinary ground to collect "compensation in advance of services to be performed and failing, upon demand, to account for or render" an accounting of such advance payment.

question: A broker deposits a buyer's security deposit into the same operating account he uses to pay his own office expenses, rather than a dedicated escrow or trustee account. Which § 20-320 ground does this violate?
choice_a: Making a material misrepresentation
choice_b: Failing to provide disclosures required by § 20-325c
choice_c: Commingling funds of others with the licensee's own, or failing to keep funds of others in an escrow or trustee account
choice_d: Entering an exclusive listing contract with an automatic continuation clause
explanation: Section 20-320(10) makes it a ground for discipline to engage in "commingling funds of others with the licensee's own, or failing to keep funds of others in an escrow or trustee account" — a core fiduciary/trust-fund handling violation.

question: Which § 20-320 ground functions as a broad catch-all covering conduct not specifically itemized elsewhere in the list of thirteen grounds?
choice_a: Failure to attend continuing education seminars
choice_b: Failure to display a business card at open houses
choice_c: Refusing to co-broke with another firm
choice_d: Any act or conduct which constitutes dishonest, fraudulent or improper dealing
explanation: Section 20-320(11) provides a broad catch-all ground for "any act or conduct which constitutes dishonest, fraudulent or improper dealing," reaching misconduct not captured by the more specific enumerated grounds.

question: A broker fails to give a buyer the property-condition-related disclosures that Connecticut law requires be provided in a transaction. Which § 20-320 ground for discipline specifically addresses this failure?
choice_a: Failure to provide disclosures required by § 20-325c
choice_b: Failure to deliver an instrument to the executing party
choice_c: Making a false promise likely to induce
choice_d: Engaging in business without a license
explanation: Section 20-320(12) makes it a disciplinary ground to fail "to provide any disclosure required pursuant to section 20-325c," tying license discipline directly to that separate mandatory-disclosure statute.

question: Beyond the twelve specific grounds, § 20-320(13) also authorizes discipline for what broader category of conduct?
choice_a: Failing to attend a Commission holiday luncheon
choice_b: Violating any provision of chapter 392 or any regulation adopted under it
choice_c: Declining to sponsor a new licensee
choice_d: Working more than 40 hours per week
explanation: Section 20-320(13) serves as a general catch-all, making it a ground for discipline to violate "any of the provisions of this chapter or any regulation adopted under the provisions of this chapter."

question: A Connecticut broker refers a homebuyer to a particular attorney in exchange for a fee paid by that attorney for the referral. What does § 20-320a say about this arrangement?
choice_a: It is permitted as long as the buyer is told about the fee afterward
choice_b: It is permitted only for referrals to mortgage lenders, not attorneys
choice_c: It is prohibited, and violation can result in license suspension/revocation plus a fine (up to $1,000 for a first offense)
choice_d: It is permitted if the fee is under $100
explanation: Section 20-320a prohibits real estate licensees from accepting a fee, commission, or other referral compensation for directing buyers to a specific attorney, mortgage broker, or lender; violations can lead to license suspension or revocation and a fine (up to $1,000 for a first offense).

question: Under § 20-320b, which of the following describes prohibited conduct by a real estate licensee with respect to appraisals?
choice_a: Recommending that a buyer obtain an independent home inspection
choice_b: Providing a lender with the property's public tax assessment record
choice_c: Disclosing to a seller that a comparable home recently sold for less than expected
choice_d: Refusing or intentionally failing to refer a homebuyer to a lender solely because that lender uses an appraiser whose appraisal came in below the sale contract price
explanation: Section 20-320b, together with the chapter's definition of "influencing real estate appraisals," prohibits a licensee from refusing or intentionally failing to refer a homebuyer to a lender based solely on that lender's use of an appraiser who returned a fair-market-value estimate lower than the contract price.
source_note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-320b; § 20-311 (definition of "influencing real estate appraisals")

question: A person with no Connecticut real estate license actively negotiates the sale of homes for a fee. Under § 20-325, this unlicensed activity can result in a fine of up to what amount per violation?
explanation: Section 20-325 prohibits engaging in the real estate business without a license and subjects violators to a fine of up to $5,000 per violation — a distinct, higher penalty than the $2,000 discretionary fine available against a licensed broker under § 20-320.

question: Which Connecticut statute entitles a real estate licensee to notice and an opportunity for a hearing before the Commission may suspend or revoke the license under § 20-320?
choice_a: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-325
choice_b: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-321
choice_c: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311a
choice_d: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312
explanation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-321, titled "Notice and hearing," governs the procedural due-process step the Commission must follow before it can act on the grounds listed in § 20-320.

question: If a licensee disagrees with a final disciplinary decision of the Connecticut Real Estate Commission, what recourse does Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-322 provide?
choice_a: No recourse — Commission decisions are final and unreviewable
choice_b: The right to have a different broker vote in the licensee's place
choice_c: The right to appeal the Commission's decision
choice_d: Automatic reinstatement after 30 days
explanation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-322, titled "Appeal," provides a licensee with a right to appeal a Commission decision made under the chapter's disciplinary provisions.

question: Separate from the general list of grounds in § 20-320, which statute specifically authorizes revocation of a real estate license upon the licensee's conviction of a crime?
choice_a: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-324
choice_b: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-325m
choice_c: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312
choice_d: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-323
explanation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-323, titled "Revocation of license upon conviction of crime," provides distinct statutory authority for license revocation tied specifically to a criminal conviction, alongside the general "conviction of a crime" ground listed in § 20-320(8).

question: Which Connecticut statute establishes misrepresentation by a real estate licensee as an offense carrying its own separate penalty, apart from the Commission's administrative disciplinary authority under § 20-320?
choice_a: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-324
choice_b: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311b
choice_c: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312(e)
choice_d: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-320a
explanation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-324, titled "Misrepresentation; penalty," imposes a penalty for misrepresentation as a standalone statutory offense, distinct from the Commission's power under § 20-320 to suspend or revoke a license for material misrepresentation.

question: How is the Connecticut Real Estate Commission composed under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311a?
choice_a: Five members elected by licensed brokers statewide
choice_b: Eight Governor-appointed members: three licensed real estate brokers, two licensed real estate salespersons, and three public members
choice_c: Three members, all licensed brokers, appointed by the Commissioner of Consumer Protection
choice_d: Twelve members, one from each real estate trade association in the state
explanation: Section 20-311a establishes an eight-member commission, all electors of the state appointed by the Governor, consisting of three licensed real estate brokers, two licensed real estate salespersons, and three public members, with political-party and congressional-district balance requirements.

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311b, what is one of the Commission's core administrative responsibilities?
choice_a: Setting the commission rate that all brokers in the state must charge
choice_b: Approving every individual real estate listing before it can be advertised
choice_c: Authorizing the Department of Consumer Protection to issue licenses and administering the chapter's provisions on licensure, renewal, suspension, and revocation
choice_d: Collecting property transfer taxes on behalf of municipalities
explanation: Section 20-311b charges the Commission with authorizing DCP to issue licenses and with administering the chapter's provisions regarding licensure and the issuance, renewal, suspension, or revocation of licenses.

question: An associate broker in Connecticut runs a print advertisement for a listing. Under § 20-312c(d), what must that advertisement prominently include?
choice_a: The associate broker's personal cell phone number only
choice_b: A disclaimer that the ad was not reviewed by the Commission
choice_c: The MLS number in bold, 14-point font
choice_d: The name of the supervising licensee who controls and supervises the associate broker
explanation: Section 20-312c(d) requires an associate broker to comply with all advertising requirements applicable to real estate brokers and to "include the name of the supervising licensee who controls and supervises such associate broker at a prominent location in all of such associate broker's advertisements."

question: A group of salespersons in Connecticut brands itself as "The Summit Home Team" and advertises together. Under § 20-312(g), what must the team's advertisements prominently include?
choice_a: The name of the team's supervising licensee
choice_b: A photo of every team member
choice_c: The team's total sales volume for the prior year
choice_d: Nothing beyond what an individual salesperson's ad requires
explanation: Section 20-312(g) requires a team to comply with all advertising requirements applicable to real estate brokers and to "include the name of such team's supervising licensee at a prominent location in all of such team's advertisements."

question: A real estate team in Connecticut wants to call itself "Summit Realty Group, LLC." Under § 20-312(e), why is this name potentially problematic?
choice_a: Team names may not include the word "Summit" or other geographic references
choice_b: It includes terms such as "realty," "group," and "LLC" that improperly imply the team is a business entity
choice_c: Teams are prohibited from having any name other than the members' individual full legal names
choice_d: The name is too long under Commission regulations
explanation: Section 20-312(e) prohibits a team name from including terms such as "associates," "company," "corporation," "group," "LLC," "real estate," or "realty" that imply the team itself is a business entity, since a team operates under its supervising broker rather than as its own licensed entity.

question: Which Connecticut statute imposes recordkeeping obligations on real estate brokers and leasing agents regarding the retention, format, and disclosure of certain real estate transaction records?
choice_a: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-320b
choice_b: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-322
choice_c: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-325m
choice_d: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311a
explanation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-325m, titled "Real estate brokers and leasing agents to retain certain records. Format and disclosure," is the statute governing brokers' and leasing agents' obligations to retain specified real estate transaction records.
